history.content: what is the legal age for a job

The legal working age varies depending on the country and the type of work. In Australia, it mostly starts at 15, while in New Zealand, it's 16 with restricted working hours and 18 for full-time unrestricted work. In Kenya, the legal working age is 13 for easy work, 16 for restricted working hours and type of work, and 18 for unrestricted work. In South Africa, it's 15 for restricted working hours and type of work, and 18 for unrestricted work. In China, the minimum employment age is 16, and no child worker or worker aged 16 or 17 is permitted to do potentially dangerous or hazardous work. In Iran, the minimum employment age is 18 for hard work, and 21 for unrestricted work. In Japan, the minimum employment age is 15, and workers aged 18 are restricted by labor laws, while at 20, work is unrestricted. In Malaysia, the minimum employment age is 14 for easy work and 16 for unrestricted work. In Indonesia, it's 13 for minimum employment age, 15 for restricted working hours and type of work, and 18 for unrestricted work. In the Philippines, it's 15 for restricted working hours and type of work, and 18 for unrestricted work. In Singapore, the minimum legal age for working is 13, with different restrictions based on age. In Thailand, the legal working age depends on the type of work and whether it interferes with school education. In Vietnam, the legal working age is 15. In Switzerland, the legal working age is 13 for easy work with parental permission, and there are different restrictions based on age up to 18, when work becomes unrestricted. In the United Kingdom, the legal working age is 13 for restricted part-time work, 16 for full-time work and to claim legal minimum wage, and 18 to work at a licensed premises that primarily sells alcoholic beverages. In Norway, the legal working age is 13 for light work with parental permission, 15 for restricted working hours and type of work, and 18 for unrestricted work. I can tell you that in most states in the United States, children are required to attend school from the age of six or seven until they turn 18. Some states allow students to leave school at 16 or 17. According to Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, Children can not be asked to leave school or be forced to repeat a class , till they complete class 8. Depending on the state, if the child is at the age of the compulsory education, they are no longer required by law to attend school.
what is definition of Child labour and what has caused Child labour? I want to understand tis clearly since I am still a child but want to start working so bad

Child labour is defined as the employment of children in any work that deprives them of their childhood, interferes with their ability to attend regular school, and is mentally, physically, socially, or morally dangerous and harmful. This practice is considered exploitative by many international organizations. According to the International Labour Organization (ILO), poverty is the greatest single cause behind child labour. For impoverished households, income from a child's work is usually crucial for his or her own survival or for that of the household. Lack of meaningful alternatives, such as affordable schools and quality education, is another major factor driving children to harmful labour. Children work because they have nothing better to do.
